# Effect: vocoder

Vocoder: shapes this track (usually synth chords) with the spectrum of another track (usually a vocal) - a singing robot.

**Where to put it**: Put it on the synth/chord track (the carrier) and set "sidechain" to the name of the vocal track or bus (the modulator). The carrier should be sustained and harmonically rich (saw pad, string machine).

Latest parameters: `muser effects vocoder` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bands` | 16 | 8 – 32 | Number of bands. 8 rough and retro; 16 normal; 32 clearer |
| `low_hz` | 100 | 40 – 16000 Hz | Lowest band |
| `high_hz` | 8000 | 40 – 16000 Hz | Highest band |
| `formant_shift` | 0 | -12 – 12 semitones | Formant shift. + higher (child, cartoon); - deeper |
| `attack_ms` | 10 | 0.1 – 500 ms | Attack time of the envelope follower |
| `release_ms` | 10 | 0.1 – 2000 ms | Release time of the envelope follower. Longer is smoother |
| `gain_db` | 0 | -24 – 24 dB | Output gain |
| `mix` | 1 | 0 – 1 | Dry/wet mix |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "vocoder", "sidechain": "voice", "bands": 16 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Classic robot choir (carrier: sawtooth pad)

  ```json
  {"type": "vocoder", "sidechain": "voice", "bands": 16}
  ```

- Vintage rough

  ```json
  {"type": "vocoder", "sidechain": "voice", "bands": 8, "release_ms": 30}
  ```

- Clear, intelligible

  ```json
  {"type": "vocoder", "sidechain": "voice", "bands": 32, "high_hz": 10000}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Put it on the **carrier** track (synth chords, string machine, sawtooth pad); `sidechain` names the **modulator** signal: a voice (an audio track) or any rhythmic track.
- The modulator track is often set to `"muted": true`: it only shapes the sound and makes no sound of its own (the sidechain still gets its signal).
- The carrier must keep sounding and be rich in overtones; when the carrier stops the vocoder is silent. Chords change along with the notes the voice sings.
- When the modulator is a calibrated built-in instrument, gain_db 0 is about as loud as the original; when a vocal recording is on the quiet side, raise gain_db.
